verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core app runs entirely on the user's own device: notes are local plain-text Markdown files that work offline and stay under the user's control. Sync can also run through user-chosen services such as Git, Dropbox or iCloud instead of Obsidian's servers. However, the first-party Sync and Publish services are hosted by Obsidian, and the app is closed-source, so there is no documented way to self-host the product's own server components. Missing for 10: a self-hostable Sync or Publish server, open-source or self-deployable core, and hands-on self-hosting documentation.
